title: synthetic_hs shows a spherical subpopulation that fails 3.12 µm channels
summary: synthetic_hs contains a high-sphericity subpopulation (39% of cells) whose surface-to-volume ratio is too low to pass narrow channels; this is compatible with a spherocytic phenotype, to be confirmed. Proposed test: constrictions at 2.87, 3.12, 3.37 µm with 18 cells per sample.

findings.text: 39% of cells in synthetic_hs have a sphericity index above 0.8 (INFERRED SI; threshold is a HYPOTHESIS), versus 1% in synthetic_healthy.

This subpopulation has a median minimum cylindrical diameter of 3.53 µm versus 3.03 µm for the rest of synthetic_hs (COMPUTED): with less surface for its volume it cannot fold into a 3 µm capsule; 97% of it is BLOCKED at 3 µm.

D50 (width where half the cells pass without stretch) is 3.16 µm for synthetic_hs versus 2.99 µm for synthetic_healthy (COMPUTED). At 3.12 µm the model predicts 87% passage for synthetic_healthy and 43% for synthetic_hs.
Worst cell c275 is BLOCKED at 3.12 µm: it would need 22% area strain, beyond the 3% lysis limit (COMPUTED). A 2x stiffness (HYPOTHESIS) cannot change a geometric BLOCKED verdict.
CBC flag for synthetic_hs: RDW-CV 17.5% (CONSTRAINED) vs 9.76% implied by the image diameters (MEASURED): the smear may under-represent the size spread; to be confirmed on another field.

consistency_flags.note: Approximation V∝D³; smear artefacts widen the image CV.

experiment.hypothesis: At 3.12 µm, synthetic_healthy passes at 87% vs synthetic_hs at 43%, driven by surface-to-volume ratio alone.
experiment.falsified_if: Measured pass fractions do not differ, or the difference disappears after osmotic swelling/shrinking controls.
caveats: Model assumes cylindrical channels; rectangular microfluidic channels need an equivalent-diameter correction.
Stiffness is not modelled; rigid cells may fail where geometry allows passage.

limitations: Sphericity is inferred from central pallor (linear map: pallor ratio 0.4 gives SI 0.74, no pallor gives SI 0.92); validated only on annotated data.
No mechanical simulation: capsule model in rigid cylindrical channels; stiffness is never predicted from images.
Synthetic samples and demo CBC values, not patient data.
